attacks.claim: The beta results (0 lost saves, 11 conflict prompts) are reported as finished, but the beta window (Nov 18-30) has not happened as of today (2026-10-26). The 'players never lose a save' commitment therefore has no real-player evidence behind it. The Epic side is the thinnest: QA ran only on an Epic dev sandbox with 150 testers, yet about 29% of players are on Epic.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch on Steam (2,300 players) and Epic sandbox testers (150). 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players."

attacks.claim: The stored-data statement says no name data is stored, but sync.meta includes a free-text device name that is uploaded and often contains a real name. The privacy disclosure, which counsel reviewed as PP-v6, is inaccurate unless device name is listed or dropped. Device name is also not validated or length-limited before it is rendered.
attacks.evidence: "`sync.meta` sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)" vs "We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, `sync.meta`. No email, name, payment or friends data."

attacks.claim: The public patch note says saves on this PC stay where they are. The sync rules silently download a newer cloud copy over an older local slot when only the cloud changed. The replaced local copy is kept in backups, but the note is inaccurate and cannot be retracted once posted.
attacks.evidence: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are." vs "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older."

attacks.claim: The automatic budget-stop kill switch and the 1.3 downgrade on the Epic store are not covered by any QA row. The downgrade was tested only on a Steam beta branch. The kill-switch flip also depends on lagging billing data and a 10-minute client poll.
attacks.evidence: "at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically"; "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)"

attacks.claim: Server retention of 5 versions and local retention of 3 give a short recovery window if a bad but valid save is synced repeatedly. The server also accepts uploads without validation. Client behaviour on 429/503 (retry and backoff) is not specified.
attacks.evidence: "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot"; "60 uploads per hour per player"

attacks.claim: Several hardening details are not stated: server-side enforcement of the under-13 restriction, link handshake state/nonce binding, and authorization for unlink-and-delete. The artifact describes server-side validation of both store sessions and scoped tokens, so these are gaps to confirm rather than demonstrated flaws.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side cabined check on the link endpoint; state/nonce binding for linking; authorization for unlink

attacks.claim: The storage forecast (140 GB) does not reconcile with 420 KB × 5 versions × 60% of 182k players, and the load test (30k launches) is smaller than the full-population patch-day launch. Cost impact is small at the stated figures.
attacks.evidence: "~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month."
